docs.title: OpenSim AI Stack Documentation
docs.text:
Welcome to the documentation suite for the OpenSim AI Docker stack.

This guide is written for people who enjoy games and virtual worlds, but may be new to OpenSimulator, Docker, or AI tooling.

Experimental project

This stack is still in active development. Back up your regions and configuration before trying major changes.

docs.title: What this stack is
docs.text:
The OpenSim AI Stack is a Docker Compose deployment that combines:

  • OpenSimulator (the virtual world server)
  • MariaDB (persistent data)
  • opensim-console2mcp (admin command bridge)
  • opensim-metaverse2mcp (in-world bot bridge)
  • opensim-opencode (AI runtime and provider integration)

docs.title: Top 10 most significant features
docs.text:
1. Natural-language server administration through OpenSimulator console commands.
  2. In-world bot avatar you can chat with by IM.
  3. Bot movement tools: walk, fly, teleport, and stop actions.
  4. Prim building tools: create, scale, rotate, texture, link, and inspect.
  5. Inventory and asset workflows (upload, download, give, and policy control).
  6. Environment controls for region and parcel lighting/weather profiles.
  7. Runtime AI provider and model switching using star commands.
  8. Prompt layering with project and in-world AGENTS.md support.
  9. Optional in-world dialog bridge for AI questions and approvals.
  10. Two runtime modes (source/release) with shared operational model.

docs.title: Choose your path
docs.text:
• If you are new to Docker and OpenSim, start with Beginner Guide -> Quick Start.
  • If you are already comfortable with containers and operations, start with Advanced Guide -> Quick Start and Modes.

docs.title: Docker learning resources
docs.text:
If Docker is new to you, these short resources are a good starting point:

  • Docker overview: https://docs.docker.com/get-started/docker-overview/
  • Docker Compose intro: https://docs.docker.com/compose/
  • Common Docker CLI reference: https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/

docs.title: OpenSimulator container
docs.text: Runs your region simulator and exposes the world endpoint (default 9000 TCP/UDP). It is initialized with values from .env through the opensim-init service.

docs.title: opensim-console2mcp
docs.text: Bridges OpenSimulator REST console endpoints into MCP tools so AI can issue admin and maintenance commands.

docs.title: opensim-metaverse2mcp
docs.text: Logs in the bot avatar and exposes movement, building, inventory, environment, and chat-linked AI control over MCP HTTP.

docs.title: opensim-opencode
docs.text: Runs Opencode server mode and uses generated opencode.json to connect to both MCP services.

docs.title: Advanced AI Configuration
docs.text: The bot supports live configuration in IM through star commands, plus startup defaults through environment variables.

docs.title: Star commands for runtime control
docs.text:
List providers and models:

*providers
*providers configured
*models
*models <provider>

Authenticate provider:

*auth methods <provider>
*auth <provider> api <api-key>
*auth <provider> oauth 0
*auth <provider> oauth-complete 0

Select provider/model:

*configure <provider-name-or-id>
*configure model <provider/model-id>
*configure thinking <low|medium|high|off>
*configure reset

Session controls:

*session create My Build Session
*session list
*session use <session-id>
*session summarize current
*session delete <session-id> --force

docs.title: Startup defaults via environment
docs.text:
Useful metaverse/opencode variables:

  • OPENCODE_INITIAL_PROVIDER
  • OPENCODE_INITIAL_MODEL
  • OPENCODE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
  • OPENCODE_HANDLER_FIRSTNAME
  • OPENCODE_HANDLER_LASTNAME
  • PROMPT_HANDLING_ENABLED
  • PROMPT_PROJECT_AGENTS_ENABLED
  • PROMPT_PROJECT_AGENTS_FILE

docs.title: MCP endpoint wiring
docs.text:
Main generated values in opencode.json are sourced from:

  • OPENCODE_MCP_URL (console MCP)
  • OPENCODE_METAVERSE_MCP_URL (metaverse MCP)

Default in-stack endpoints:

  • http://opensim-console2mcp:8997/mcp
  • http://opensim-metaverse2mcp:8999/mcp

docs.title: Adding more MCP servers
docs.text:
You can extend opencode.json with additional remote MCP servers.

Example pattern:

{
  "mcp": {
    "local_host_mcp": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "http://opensim-console2mcp:8997/mcp",
      "enabled": true
    },
    "metaverse_mcp": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "http://opensim-metaverse2mcp:8999/mcp",
      "enabled": true
    },
    "extra_tools": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "http://my-extra-mcp:8080/mcp",
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}

Prefer runtime changes first

Use star commands for day-to-day provider/model switches. Use env or opencode.json for stable baseline defaults.

docs.title: Environment payload workflow
docs.text:
1. Pull baseline payload.
  2. Edit only required values.
  3. Apply raw JSON payload.

Prompt example:

Get region environment, reduce cloud shadow, then apply updated region environment.

Minimal payload shape example:

{
  "day_length": 14400,
  "day_offset": 57600,
  "flags": 0,
  "day_cycle": {

    "tracks": []

Use baseline-first edits

docs.title: Advanced Hardening
docs.text: Default settings are convenient for local testing, not public exposure.

docs.title: Credentials you should change
docs.text:
Update these in .env before opening ports to the internet:

  • OPENSIM_ESTATE_OWNER_PASSWORD
  • OPENSIM_CONSOLE_USER
  • OPENSIM_CONSOLE_PASS
  • MARIADB_PASSWORD
  • MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD
  • OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD
  • OPENCODE_PASSWORD (if using Basic auth path)

docs.title: API and transport hardening
docs.text:
• Set METAVERSE_MCP_HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN to protect metaverse MCP endpoint.
  • Use strong credentials for Opencode server auth paths.
  • Restrict host firewall exposure to only required ports.
  • Keep private services on Docker internal network when possible.

docs.title: Bot control hardening
docs.text:
Use handler restrictions:

  • OPENCODE_HANDLER_FIRSTNAME
  • OPENCODE_HANDLER_LASTNAME

Use dialog bridge trust restrictions:

  • OPENCODE_LSL_DIALOG_BRIDGE_TRUSTED_OWNER_ID
  • OPENCODE_LSL_DIALOG_BRIDGE_TRUSTED_OBJECT_ID
  • OPENCODE_LSL_DIALOG_BRIDGE_REQUIRE_TRUSTED_SENDER=true

docs.title: Password change operations after deployment
docs.text:
Reset an account password through console command path:

reset user password First Last NewStrongPassword

Rotate console access credentials by updating .env, then restart affected services:

docker compose up -d

docker compose restart opensim opensim-console2mcp

docs.title: Network and host hygiene
docs.text:
• Use reverse proxy/TLS in front of exposed HTTP endpoints.
  • Keep host OS patched.
  • Back up volumes regularly before updates.
  • Pin known-good image tags for production-like environments.

docs.title: Recovery and audit basics
docs.text:
• Export OAR/IAR on a schedule.
  • Keep change logs for .env and compose overrides.
  • Test restore procedure on a non-production stack.

No hardening is one setting

Security is layered: credentials, network limits, identity controls, and backup discipline all matter together.

docs.title: Recommended operation order
docs.text:
1. Inspect current state (ParcelGetCurrent, EstateGetInfo).
  2. Apply minimal change (ParcelSetInfo, ParcelSetLanding, TerrainTerraform).
  3. Re-read state and confirm behavior.
  4. Announce impact before disruptive actions (restart/schedule changes).

docs.title: Prompt examples for precise control
docs.text:
Get parcel by local ID 42 with access lists included.

Update parcel 42 name to Main Landing, set media URL to https://example.com/screen.

Set parcel 42 landing type to direct.

Run parcel permission diagnostics for parcel 42.

Join parcels in bounds west=96 south=96 east=160 north=160.

Subdivide parcels in bounds west=96 south=96 east=128 north=128.

Sample terrain heights with step 8 and report missing cache points.

Terraform parcel 42 with action smooth and brush large.

Export terrain heightmap to /workspace/state/region-terrain.r32

Import terrain heightmap from /workspace/state/region-terrain.r32

Verify terrain patch cache at step 8 with minimum coverage ratio 0.9 and timeout 20 seconds.

Diff terrain source current vs /workspace/state/region-terrain.r32 with min delta 0.05 and max samples 20.

Apply terrain patch offset in bounds west=96 south=96 east=128 north=128 with delta 0.5 meters.

Apply terrain patch offset from /workspace/state/base-terrain.r32 in bounds west=96 south=96 east=128 north=128 with delta 0.5 meters.

Set weekly restart schedule for tue,thu at 02:15 UTC.

docs.title: Safe parcel ops playbook
docs.text:
Use this sequence to reduce mistakes and permission surprises:

  1. Inspect target parcel and permission hints.
  2. Confirm exact bounds and impact with the user.
  3. Execute one structural change (join or subdivide).
  4. Re-read parcel state and report what changed.

Example prompt sequence:

Get parcel by local ID 42 with access lists included.

Run parcel permission diagnostics for parcel 42 and summarize blockers.

Subdivide parcels in bounds west=96 south=96 east=128 north=128.

Get parcel by local ID 42 again and confirm landing, media, and access-list state.

docs.title: Notes and current limitations
docs.text:
• Terrain sampling reads simulator-cached patches; missing samples usually mean the patch cache is incomplete.
  • If cache coverage is 0%, TerrainHeightmapExportRaw now fails instead of writing a misleading all-zero file.
  • Terraform now uses a cache-safe reference-height fallback when terrain patch cache is incomplete.
  • Patch-level workflows are available: verify cache coverage, diff RAW sources, and apply bounded offsets.
  • For cache-cold sessions, prefer TerrainPatchApplyOffsetRaw with a known .r32 source file/URL.
  • Access list support is read-focused in current MCP flows.
  • Estate operations depend on simulator capabilities and your estate permission level.

Prefer capability-aware retries

If a call fails, first re-check capability availability and privileges, then retry with narrower scope.

docs.title: Animation control
docs.text:
Use AnimationsList to discover built-in animation names (e.g. DANCE1, WAVE, CLAP, SIT), then start/stop them by name or raw UUID:

AnimationsList()
AnimationStart(animation="DANCE1")
ActiveAnimations()
AnimationStop(animation="DANCE1")

docs.title: Reliable navigation pattern
docs.text:
For long distances, prefer waypoint-style prompts:

Walk to 140,130,25 first, then fly to 200,200,60, then land.

This aligns with stepped autopilot behavior used by movement tools.

docs.title: Teleport targeting strategy
docs.text:
• Use explicit region names plus coordinates when possible.
  • If region name collisions exist, use a region-handle or precise routing command.
  • Confirm location with status before issuing object-edit operations.

docs.title: Operational checks
docs.text:
Health endpoint for bot runtime:

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8999/healthz

If your mapped host port is not 8999, adjust the URL.

docs.title: Failure recovery
docs.text:
• If movement hangs, send:
*cancel
Stop movement.
  • If login session is stale, restart only the metaverse sidecar:
docker compose restart opensim-metaverse2mcp

Handler-gated control

If handler restrictions are enabled, only the configured handler avatar can issue bot control commands.

docs.title: Advanced Quick Start and Modes
docs.text: This guide focuses on mode selection, image strategy, and operational commands.

docs.title: Build modes
docs.text:
• Source mode: uses docker-compose.yml and OPENSIM_SOURCE_IMAGE by default.
  • Release mode: uses docker-compose.release.yml and OPENSIM_RELEASE_IMAGE by default.

Both modes include the same sidecars (opensim-console2mcp, opensim-metaverse2mcp, opensim-opencode) and MariaDB.

docs.title: Compose entry points
docs.text:
Published images:

docker compose up -d
docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml up -d

Local build helper scripts:

./run.sh
./run-release.sh

Local override files

Helper scripts use docker-compose.local.yml or docker-compose.release.local.yml to build local images while keeping compose wiring consistent.

docs.title: Minimal environment baseline
docs.text:
At minimum, set:

  • OPENSIM_HOSTNAME
  • OPENSIM_REGION_PORT
  • OPENSIM_CONSOLE_USER
  • OPENSIM_CONSOLE_PASS
  • OPENSIM_ESTATE_OWNER_PASSWORD

For sidecars, verify:

  • MCP_PORT
  • METAVERSE_MCP_PORT
  • OPENCODE_PORT
  • OPENSIM_LOGIN_FIRSTNAME
  • OPENSIM_LOGIN_LASTNAME
  • OPENSIM_LOGIN_PASSWORD

docs.title: Service topology checks
docs.text:
Get status:

docker compose ps

Tail logs for key services:

docker compose logs -f opensim

docker compose logs -f opensim-console2mcp

docker compose logs -f opensim-metaverse2mcp

docker compose logs -f opensim-opencode

docs.title: Regenerate first-run config
docs.text:
If REST console or bootstrap config drifted due to old volumes:

docker compose down -v

docker compose up -d

docs.title: Port mapping defaults
docs.text:
• OpenSim: 9000/tcp and 9000/udp (host side uses OPENSIM_REGION_PORT)
  • Console MCP: 8997/tcp
  • Metaverse MCP: 8999/tcp
  • Opencode HTTP: 8998/tcp

docs.title: Server Maintenance and User Management
docs.text: This page covers practical maintenance tasks that map closely to OpenSimulator console commands exposed through opensim-console2mcp.

docs.title: Region operations
docs.text:
Create a region:

create region "Region Name" Regions/RegionName.ini

Show regions:

show regions

Restart current region:

restart

Schedule restart with notice:

region restart notice "Maintenance in progress" 300 60 30

Abort a scheduled restart:

region restart abort "Restart canceled"

docs.title: User management
docs.text:
Create user:

create user First Last Password email@example.com

Show account:

show account First Last

Reset password:

reset user password First Last NewPassword

Kick user:

kick user First Last --force "Maintenance"

docs.title: Import and export resources
docs.text:
Export region to OAR:

save oar /workspace/exports/region-backup.oar

Import region from OAR:

load oar /workspace/imports/region-restore.oar

Export user inventory (IAR):

save iar First Last / Password /workspace/exports/user.iar

Import user inventory (IAR):

load iar First Last / Password /workspace/imports/user.iar

docs.title: Terrain and scene maintenance
docs.text:
Set water height:

set water height 25

Backup pending object changes:

backup

Show scene stats:

show scene

docs.title: Runtime operations from Docker host
docs.text:
Restart one service:

docker compose restart opensim

Restart full stack:

docker compose restart

Inspect recent logs:

docker compose logs --tail 200 opensim

High-impact commands

Commands like load oar, object deletion, or scene transforms can be destructive. Take backups first.

docs.title: Advanced Social, Groups, and Session Control
docs.text: This page covers group-focused MCP workflows: membership visibility, group chat/session control, role/title management, and group notices.

docs.title: Group discovery and profile tools
docs.text:
• GroupListCurrent
  • GroupGetProfile
  • GroupGetMembers
  • GroupGetRoles
  • GroupGetRoleMembers
  • GroupGetTitles

Use includeDetails=false for fast summaries and includeDetails=true when you need full payloads.

docs.title: Group chat/session tools
docs.text:
• GroupChatJoin
  • GroupChatLeave
  • GroupChatSend
  • GroupChatSessionsList
  • GroupChatAcceptInvite

Operational notes:

  • GroupChatSend requires an active tracked session; join first if needed.
  • GroupChatJoin supports waitForJoinSeconds (0 = fire-and-forget, >0 = wait for GroupChatJoined).
  • GroupChatSessionsList with includeDetails=true surfaces per-member moderation/voice flags.

docs.title: Role/title action tools
docs.text:
• GroupSetActive
  • GroupSetActiveTitle
  • GroupRoleCreate
  • GroupRoleUpdate
  • GroupRoleDelete
  • GroupRoleAddMember
  • GroupRoleRemoveMember

Verification notes:

  • GroupRoleAddMember and GroupRoleRemoveMember support verifyAfterSubmit and verifyWaitSeconds.
  • When verification is enabled, tools classify outcomes as confirmed vs submitted-but-unverified.

docs.title: Structured role payload (Option B)
docs.text:
GroupRoleCreate and GroupRoleUpdate accept this object schema:

{
  "name": "Builder",
  "title": "Builder",
  "description": "Can edit and maintain builds",
  "powers": "ObjectManipulate,ObjectSetForSale"
}

powers supports either:

  • comma/pipe-separated GroupPowers enum names, or
  • numeric bitmask string.

docs.title: Group invite and ban tools
docs.text:
• GroupInviteUser
  • GroupBanListGet
  • GroupBanSet

docs.title: Structured invite payload
docs.text:
{
  "targetAgentId": "99999999-8888-7777-6666-555555555555",
  "roleIdsCsv": null,
  "useEveryoneRoleIfEmpty": true
}

docs.title: Structured ban payload
docs.text:
{
  "action": "ban",
  "agentIdsCsv": "99999999-8888-7777-6666-555555555555"
}

Ban notes:

  • GroupBanSet supports verifyAfterSubmit and verifyWaitSeconds.
  • Verification uses read-back from GroupBanListGet-equivalent state and returns classified outcomes.

docs.title: Notice tools
docs.text:
• GroupNoticesList
  • GroupNoticeSend

docs.title: Structured notice payload
docs.text:
{
  "subject": "Weekly restart",
  "message": "Region restart in 10 minutes.",
  "attachmentItemId": null,
  "attachmentOwnerId": null
}

If attachment fields are used, both IDs are required and must be UUIDs.

docs.title: Group create/update tools (structured payload)
docs.text:
• GroupCreate
  • GroupUpdate

docs.title: Structured group payload (Option B)
docs.text:
{
  "name": "OpenSim Builders",
  "charter": "Collaborative build group",
  "insigniaId": null,
  "membershipFee": 0,
  "openEnrollment": true,
  "showInList": true,
  "allowPublish": false,
  "maturePublish": false
}

docs.title: Suggested execution order
docs.text:
1. Query current state (GroupListCurrent, GroupGetRoles, GroupGetTitles).
  2. Apply one change (GroupRoleUpdate, GroupSetActiveTitle, or GroupNoticeSend).
  3. Re-read state to verify (GroupGetRoles/GroupGetTitles/GroupNoticesList/GroupBanListGet).
  4. For chat automation, verify active sessions with GroupChatSessionsList before sending.

docs.title: Beginner Land Basics
docs.text: This page helps you make safe land-related changes with plain-language prompts.

docs.title: What you can do now
docs.text:
• Read parcel details for where you are standing.
  • Update parcel name, description, music URL, and media URL.
  • Configure parcel landing point behavior.
  • View parcel allow and ban lists.
  • Sample terrain heights and run terraform actions.
  • Send region or estate broadcast messages (if your account has rights).

docs.title: Starter prompt examples
docs.text:
Show the parcel details where I am right now.

Rename this parcel to Welcome Plaza and set the description to Beginner sandbox area.

Set parcel music URL to https://example.com/radio-stream

Set this parcel landing type to landing point at 128,128,25.

Show the ban list for parcel local ID 42.

docs.title: Terrain examples
docs.text:
Sample terrain heights every 16 meters.

Smooth terrain on parcel 42 with a medium brush.

Terraform is destructive

Terraform changes modify land shape. Test in sandboxes first and confirm permissions before running large edits.

docs.title: Estate/admin examples
docs.text:
Show estate info for this region.

Broadcast message to this region: Scheduled restart in 10 minutes.

Set weekly restart schedule for mon,wed,fri at 03:30 UTC.

docs.title: Good safety habits
docs.text:
1. Ask the bot to read current parcel details before editing.
  2. Change one property at a time so rollbacks are easier.
  3. Use clear restart notices before scheduling or triggering restarts.

For low-level tool names and exact operation patterns, see Advanced Guide -> Land Management.

docs.title: Beginner Movement and Animation
docs.text: These examples are natural-language prompts you can send to the bot in IM.

docs.title: Basic movement prompts
docs.text:
Walk to me.

Move 5 meters forward.

Fly to me and land.

Stop moving.

docs.title: Teleport prompts
docs.text:
Teleport to region Welcome Island at 128,128,25.

Teleport back to my current region.

Use clear targets

Give region name plus coordinates when possible. It reduces ambiguity and failed teleports.

docs.title: Animation prompts
docs.text:
Wave at me.

Play the dance animation.

Start clapping.

Stop all animations.

What animations are you playing?

Use built-in animation names

Names like wave, dance, clap, bow, laugh, and sit resolve to the viewer's built-in animations. You can also pass an animation UUID directly.

docs.title: Follow-and-demonstrate workflow
docs.text:
1. Ask the bot to come near you.
  2. Ask it to fly to a point.
  3. Ask it to stop.
  4. Ask it to return.

Example sequence:

Walk to me.
Fly to 140,130,45.
Stop movement.
Walk back to 128,128,25.

docs.title: Troubleshooting movement and animation
docs.text:
• If the bot does not respond, confirm you are messaging the correct avatar.
  • If commands lag, check container health and logs.
  • If teleport fails, verify the destination region exists and is online.
  • If an animation does not play, check that the name is a known built-in animation or provide a valid animation UUID.

For tool-level details, see Advanced Guide -> Movement and Navigation.

docs.title: Beginner AI Permissions and Questions
docs.text: The bot may ask permission before doing sensitive actions (file edits, command execution, or risky operations).

docs.title: Two ways prompts appear
docs.text:
1. In IM chat (default and always available).
  2. In optional in-world popup dialogs via the LSL dialog bridge.

The dialog bridge is a small script object (dialog-bridge.lsl) that can show multiple-choice prompts using llDialog.

docs.title: Essential star commands
docs.text:
List pending permission requests:

*permission list

Allow a request:

*permission allow <permission-id>

Deny a request:

*permission deny <permission-id>

List pending questions:

*question list

Answer a question:

*question answer <question-id> <your answer>

Reject a question:

*question reject <question-id>

docs.title: Prompt visibility commands
docs.text:
*prompt status
*prompt show effective
*prompt reload-project

docs.title: Safety defaults to know
docs.text:
• Permission prompts are interactive by design.
  • Handler restrictions can limit who may control the bot.
  • Dialog bridge trust checks can require known sender object/owner IDs.

If you are stuck

Run *status and then *permission list to see if the bot is waiting for your approval.

docs.title: Beginner Quick Start
docs.text: This path is for first-time users who want a working local stack with minimal setup.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker Engine
  • Docker Compose v2 (docker compose)
  • An OpenSimulator viewer (Firestorm is commonly used)

New to Docker?

Start with Docker's short guides before continuing: https://docs.docker.com/get-started/docker-overview/

docs.title: 1) Prepare your environment file
docs.text:
From the opensim-ai-docker repository:

cp .env.example .env

Set at least OPENSIM_HOSTNAME in .env.

Minimal values to review before first run:

  • OPENSIM_HOSTNAME
  • OPENSIM_REGION_PORT
  • OPENSIM_ESTATE_OWNER_FIRST
  • OPENSIM_ESTATE_OWNER_LAST
  • OPENSIM_ESTATE_OWNER_PASSWORD
  • OPENSIM_CONSOLE_USER
  • OPENSIM_CONSOLE_PASS

docs.title: 2) Start the stack
docs.text:
Source-mode compose (default):

docker compose up -d

Release-mode compose:

docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml up -d

docs.title: 3) Log in with your viewer
docs.text:
Use these credentials unless you changed them in .env:

  • Username: Admin User
  • Password: changeme

Grid/login URL normally uses your region endpoint, for example:

http://<OPENSIM_HOSTNAME>:<OPENSIM_REGION_PORT>

Viewer grid manager

Some viewers need you to manually add a custom grid. Look for "Grid Manager" or "Preferences -> Grids" in your viewer settings.

docs.title: 4) Start your first conversation with the bot
docs.text:
After login, find Bot User and open an IM conversation.

Try this first command:

Place a cube prim 2 meters away and scale it x2.

Then try simple movement:

Walk to me.

docs.title: 5) Optional: pick a stronger model
docs.text:
Use star commands in IM:

*auth methods github-copilot
*auth github-copilot oauth 0
*auth github-copilot oauth-complete 0
*configure github-copilot/gpt-5.3-codex

If your provider needs API keys instead, see Advanced Guide -> AI Configuration.

docs.title: 6) Stop and reset commands
docs.text:
Stop services:

docker compose down

Full wipe including persistent volumes:

docker compose down -v

Data loss

down -v removes region/database state for this stack invocation.

docs.title: Beginner Social and Groups
docs.text: This page helps you use group features in plain language with safe, incremental prompts.

docs.title: What you can do now
docs.text:
• List the groups your bot is currently in.
  • Join and leave group chat sessions.
  • Send group chat messages after joining a session.
  • View group members, roles, titles, and notices.
  • Send a group notice (with optional attachment IDs).
  • Set active group and active group title.
  • Invite avatars to a group.
  • View and manage group bans (if your role has permission).

docs.title: Starter prompts
docs.text:
Show my current groups.

Join group chat for group UUID 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555.

Send to group chat 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555: Hello everyone.

List group members for 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555.

List group notices for 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555.

Send a group notice to 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555 with subject Weekly Meeting and message Meeting starts in 10 minutes.

Invite avatar 99999999-8888-7777-6666-555555555555 to group 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555 using the Everyone role.

Show banned agents for group 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555.

Ban avatar 99999999-8888-7777-6666-555555555555 from group 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555 and verify the result.

docs.title: Role and title examples
docs.text:
Set my active group to 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555.

Set my active title role in group 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555 to role UUID aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee.

Add member 99999999-8888-7777-6666-555555555555 to role aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee in group 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555.

docs.title: Good safety habits
docs.text:
1. Start with read operations (groups, members, roles, notices) before changing roles or titles.
  2. Use UUID copy/paste carefully; one typo can target the wrong group.
  3. Send a short test notice before sending an important estate-wide announcement.
  4. Use verification-enabled prompts for role and ban changes when possible.

For exact tool names and structured role/group payloads, see Advanced Guide -> Social, Groups, and Session Control.

docs.title: Architecture Diagram
docs.text:
This diagram shows how the stack components fit together, including the database, hypergrid, dialog bridge, and external AI provider/model.

%%{init: {'flowchart': {'nodeSpacing': 55, 'rankSpacing': 110, 'diagramPadding': 16}}}%%
flowchart TB
    User["Viewer user"] -->|"IM commands"| BotAvatar["Bot avatar in OpenSimulator"]

    subgraph DockerHost["Docker Compose Stack"]
      direction TB

      subgraph OpenSimSide["OpenSim Side"]
        direction LR
        OpenSim["opensim container - OpenSimulator runtime"]
        DB[(MariaDB)]
        OpenSimInit["opensim-init config bootstrap"]
      end

      subgraph MCPBridgeSide["MCP Bridge Side"]
        direction LR
        ConsoleMCP["opensim-console2mcp MCP HTTP"]
        MetaMCP["opensim-metaverse2mcp MCP HTTP and bot session"]
      end

      subgraph AISide["AI Side"]
        direction LR
        OpenCode["opensim-opencode Opencode server"]
        OpenCodeInit["opensim-opencode-init generated opencode.json"]
      end
    end

    Hypergrid["Hypergrid destinations"] <-->|"teleports"| OpenSim
    OpenSimInit --> OpenSim
    OpenSim --> DB

    OpenSim -->|"REST console"| ConsoleMCP
    MetaMCP -->|"bot login and world actions"| OpenSim

    OpenCodeInit --> OpenCode
    OpenCode <-->|"MCP tools"| ConsoleMCP
    OpenCode <-->|"MCP tools"| MetaMCP

    Provider["AI provider and model (GitHub Copilot, OpenAI, local)"] <-->|"API auth and model calls"| OpenCode

    DialogBridge["LSL dialog bridge object (optional)"] <-->|"private chat protocol"| MetaMCP
    DialogBridge -->|"llDialog prompts"| User

docs.title: Data flow summary
docs.text:
1. You send bot instructions via in-world IM.
  2. opensim-metaverse2mcp routes the text to Opencode chat sessions.
  3. Opencode decides which MCP tools to call.
  4. Tool calls go to either opensim-console2mcp (server admin) or opensim-metaverse2mcp (in-world actions).
  5. Results return back through Opencode and are sent to you in-world.

Bridge script is optional

The LSL dialog bridge is optional. Without it, permission questions still appear in IM and can be answered with star commands.

docs.title: opensim-ai-docker
docs.text:
Main composition repository that orchestrates all services.

Primary files:

  • docker-compose.yml (source mode)
  • docker-compose.release.yml (release mode)
  • .env.example
  • run.sh / run-release.sh

docs.title: opensim + opensim-init
docs.text:
• opensim-init generates first-run config from environment variables.
  • opensim runs the OpenSimulator runtime.
  • REST console endpoints are expected on the simulator HTTP endpoint.

docs.title: opensim-console2mcp
docs.text:
• Bridges OpenSimulator REST console to MCP.
  • Typical in-stack endpoint: http://opensim-console2mcp:8997/mcp.
  • Key inputs: OPENSIM_CONSOLE_URL, OPENSIM_CONSOLE_USER, OPENSIM_CONSOLE_PASS.

docs.title: opensim-metaverse2mcp
docs.text:
• Logs bot avatar into the grid.
  • Exposes movement/building/inventory/environment tools over MCP HTTP.
  • Handles IM-driven star commands for sessions, provider auth, and runtime configuration.

docs.title: opensim-opencode-init and opensim-opencode
docs.text:
• Init service writes stack opencode.json with MCP wiring.
  • Opencode service runs server mode and executes tool-using AI sessions.

docs.title: Data and volume model
docs.text:
Common persistent volumes include:

  • opensim-mariadb
  • opensim-workspace
  • opensim-config
  • opensim-assetcache
  • opensim-maptiles
  • opencode-data
  • opencode-state
  • opencode-cache
  • opencode-config

docs.text:

docs.title: Metaverse and OpenSimulator terms
docs.text:
Avatar A user representation in a virtual world.

Region A simulator-hosted area of the world (often 256m x 256m in classic setups).

Grid A collection of regions and shared services (users, inventory, assets).

Hypergrid Protocol for teleporting between independent OpenSim-compatible grids.

Estate Administrative grouping of region settings and ownership controls.

Prim Basic 3D building block object used to create structures.

IAR Inventory Archive file format for user inventory export/import.

OAR OpenSimulator Archive file format for full region export/import.

docs.title: AI and MCP terms
docs.text:
AI provider Service that hosts models (for example, cloud or local model providers).

Model Specific AI engine used to process prompts and generate tool actions.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) Protocol for exposing tools and resources to AI runtimes.

Tool call A structured action request made by AI to an MCP server.

Prompt layer One source of instruction text (built-in, project AGENTS.md, or in-world notecard).

Star command Chat command prefixed with * used by the bot for runtime control.

docs.title: Stack-specific terms
docs.text:
opensim-console2mcp Service that bridges OpenSim REST console commands to MCP.

opensim-metaverse2mcp Service that controls the bot avatar and exposes in-world tools over MCP.

opensim-opencode Containerized Opencode server used as the AI runtime in this stack.

Dialog bridge Optional LSL script object that shows AI questions as in-world popup dialogs.

Handler avatar Configured avatar identity allowed to control the bot when handler restrictions are enabled.
